title: ewo-championship
label: “The Dealer” Dylan Dunn

won.source: The 2007 Hall of Fame page’s own reign line: "Dylan Dunn — eWo World Heavyweight Champion (1)" (/promotions/ewo/archive/hall-of-fame.html).

how: Held under the title's own earlier name, eWo World Heavyweight Champion; the surviving record doesn't say from whom or when, only that it comes after Bill Dynamite's own explicitly-marked first reign.

title: ewo-championship
label: "The Idol" Bill Dynamite

won.source: The promotion’s own About page: "Dynamite was able to defeat Dunn, to become the first eWo Champion" (/promotions/ewo/archive/about.html).

how: Beat Dylan Dunn two falls to one in the tournament final that crowned eWo's first champion, at the promotion's own first pay-per-view; refereed by Erin Jacobs.
note: The Hall of Fame page's own [First] marker confirms this as the belt's founding reign.

title: ewo-championship
label: Czecher

won.source: The Legend’s own roster card: "he was faced with a challenge at eWo’s first PPV: Hell & Back. He was to face Czecher, C.M. Vyrus, and James Dean for his eWo Championship... Legend’s 117 day streak as champion was brought to an end as Czecher pinned James Dean to become the new eWo Champion" (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

how: Won a four-way match at Hell & Back — eWo's first pay-per-view of its second run — pinning James Dean rather than champion The Legend, ending Legend's 117-day reign.
note: Hell & Back is not itself a held document; this account survives only in The Legend's own roster-card retrospective. Reconciles the Hall of Fame page's bare 'eWo Champion (1)' credit to Czecher with an era and a mechanism.

title: ewo-championship
label: The Legend

won.source: The promotion’s own About page narrates Cody Clark handing Legend the belt at BWF Danger Zone 2007 (/promotions/ewo/archive/about.html); The Legend’s own roster card: "Legend entered Epic Wrestling Organization as champion... named the first eWo Champion in the process" (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

how: Awarded the vacant eWo Championship by chairman Cody Clark at BWF Danger Zone 2007, in the ring, moments after Legend's own last match as BWF Champion — the event the fed's own history calls the start of 'the second coming of eWo.' His first defense, per his own roster card, was against the last LWA Champion, Xaria Linette.
note: Lost to Czecher at Hell & Back — see the following reign.

title: ewo-championship
label: The Legend

won.source: The Legend’s own roster card: "Legend’s new finisher the Red Lottery was enough to regain his beloved eWo Championship" at Body Count (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

how: Regained the title from Czecher at Body Count with his new finisher, the Red Lottery. Defended it afterward against Erin Jacobs at Supremacy, Lawrence Jarvis at License to Thrill, and a Guilty As Charged triple threat against Alexis Sykes and Xaria Linette, then Alexis Sykes again in an Ultimate Tables Match — the fed's own account calls this the only eWo Championship reign to break 100 days twice over.
note: License to Thrill's own date is fixed by the news page's 27 August 2007 post; Guilty As Charged's by the 1 October 2007 post (/promotions/ewo/archive/news-2007.html; /promotions/ewo/archive/news-headlines-2007.html). None of Hell & Back, Body Count, Supremacy, License to Thrill or Guilty As Charged is itself a held document — every detail here survives only in The Legend's own roster-card retrospective. Lost to Frank Murdoch at The New Black, which followed Violence XIX (14 October 2007) and preceded the fed's own 25 November 2007 closure.

title: ewo-championship
label: Frank Murdoch

won.source: The Legend’s own roster card: "Legend’s 126 day reign ended when Frank Murdoch became the first man to pin Legend in eWo and becoming the NEW eWo champion" at The New Black (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

how: Won a number-one contenders match, then became the first man to pin The Legend in eWo, at The New Black, ending Legend's 126-day reign.
note: eWo closed on 25 November 2007 with no further record of the title changing hands; the closure itself is the last word on this reign. No roster card of Murdoch's own survives — known only through The Legend's and Xaria Linette's own roster-card retrospectives.

title: ewo-championship
label: C.M. Vyrus

won.source: No document records how or when Vyrus became eWo Champion. First attested as reigning champion on the front page dated 04/06/08 (/promotions/ewo/archive/front-page-2008.html), five weeks after the promotion’s own 23 March 2008 reopening; his own roster card credits him one eWo Championship reign.

how: First attested as champion on the front page's own 6 April 2008 'Champions' listing. eWo's own reopening show, The Crowning: Epic Homecoming (23 March 2008), closed on an eWo Championship triple threat match whose own chapter index names no entrants and records no result — a plausible occasion for this reign's start, but the connection is not stated anywhere in the surviving record and is not asserted here.

title: ewo-championship
label: Kyle Cross

won.source: First attested as (c) eWo Champion on the 27 April 2008 pay-per-view card, defending against The Legend (/promotions/ewo/archive/ppv-2008-04-27-card.html); his own roster card credits him one eWo Championship reign. The only match on file between C.M. Vyrus’s own 6 April 2008 listing as champion and this card is a C.M. Vyrus vs Kyle Cross singles bout on the 20 April 2008 Violence card, not labeled a title match on the card itself — a plausible but unconfirmed occasion for the change.

how: Billed as reigning eWo Champion (c) heading into There We Be Blood, 27 April 2008, defending against The Legend in the main event, an Electric Barbed Wire Ropes Match — the last title context anywhere in the surviving record. No results page for the event was captured and nothing says whether it took place.
